reasoning: metric-stream is the classic STREAM memory-bandwidth benchmark — a legitimate HPC micro-benchmark. Among the variants there are three families: (a) plain CPU STREAM (cpu, cpu-zen4, c2d, c4, azure-hpc, rocky-8, vtune, hpc7g/arm64), (b) libfabric-flavored images that still contain the same non-MPI STREAM binary (the fabric libs are irrelevant since STREAM has mpi=none and no libfabric linkage), and (c) CUDA cuda-stream builds plus the azure-hpc-ubuntu2204 image (which actually carries NCCL tests, a different application). Since the goal is to run STREAM itself and the target has no GPU requirement, I picked the generic ':cpu' image: it is the cleanest, most portable amd64 build (stream_c.exe NEEDED=[libc.so.6] only, gcc -O2), with no CUDA/driver dependency that could fail on a CPU node and no vendor-specific microarchitecture pinning (unlike cpu-zen4/c2d/c4/hpc7g, which would narrow the matchable clusters). Command is the installed C binary stream_c.exe; STREAM is a serial/OpenMP single-node kernel with no MPI, so at 3 nodes it simply runs one independent instance per exclusively-allocated node to sample per-node bandwidth — no launcher, ranks or cores specified. needs_gpu=false because capability.accelerator is 'none' and gpu_libs is empty. Network is omitted (empty): the binary links no MPI or libfabric, so any fabric (efa or plain ethernet) is acceptable and constraining it would only reduce matches. Memory 0-16GB: default STREAM arrays are ~10M doubles x3 (~240MB), and even generous rebuilds stay well under 16GB, so there is no OOM risk on a small node while keeping the footprint honest rather than over-reserving.
